A Thread Dump Names a Deadlock Cycle, Not a Thread Stuck Behind a Holder That Waits

recorded.prompt:q-heap-info-growing: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-heap-info-growing: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-heap-info-growing: The page decides c. It says "used" counts every byte in the regions handed out, "including the 142 young regions full of arrays nobody references". It also says "So a high 'used' figure is not a leak. A leak is the number after a full collection (`211M->65M` here) climbing from one collection to the next." The plain histogram "ran a stop-the-world full collection ... on a heap of tens of gigabytes it can stop the service for seconds."
recorded.prompt:q-dump-holder-reads: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-dump-holder-reads: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-dump-holder-reads: The page decides a: "A thread keeps its monitors while it parks, sleeps or reads a socket." It also says "Follow each `BLOCKED` thread's address to its `- locked` line, then read what the holder waits for. Match the address". The page uses an "HTTP request without a timeout" as the production version of the holder's wait. The page never shows a RUNNABLE holder in a socket read, but the rule above covers it.
recorded.prompt:q-reentrantlock-recording: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-reentrantlock-recording: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-reentrantlock-recording: The page decides c: "a `ReentrantLock` is not a monitor: the same ledger with one recorded no `jdk.JavaMonitorEnter` events, and its waits were `jdk.ThreadPark` events with `parkedClass = java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock$NonfairSync`."
recorded.prompt:q-container-default-heap: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-container-default-heap: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-container-default-heap: The page decides b: "In a container that is the container's limit (`UseContainerSupport` is on by default)" and "`MaxRAMPercentage` defaults to 25". The page's table has no 2g row, but its 1g->256 MB and 4g->1024 MB rows bracket it, and 25 % of 2 GB is 512 MB. The 126 MB floor applies only between about 250 and 500 MB, so it does not apply here.
recorded.prompt:q-oomkilled-under-xmx: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-oomkilled-under-xmx: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-oomkilled-under-xmx: The page decides a: "`-Xmx` limits the heap only. Thread stacks, class metadata, compiled code, the collector's own structures and direct buffers live outside it" and "the kernel charges each page to the container once it is touched". It also says "the kernel kills the process (`OOMKilled`). There is no `OutOfMemoryError` ... because the JVM never ran out of heap."

recorded.prompt:q-heap-info-growing:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-heap-info-growing:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-heap-info-growing:a: Refuted: "The plain histogram counts only live objects. To find them it ran a stop-the-world full collection." The reference table also says it "runs a full GC first".
recorded.prompt:q-heap-info-growing:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-heap-info-growing:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-heap-info-growing:b: Refuted: "used" includes garbage ("211 MB, three times what the program holds"), and "a high 'used' figure is not a leak."
recorded.prompt:q-heap-info-growing:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-heap-info-growing:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-heap-info-growing:d: The reason is refuted: "The plain histogram counts only live objects" and "`-all` collects nothing and counts garbage too." FLAG, partly true: d's advice (watch the heap left after each full collection) is the same correct advice as c. Only its stated reason is wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-dump-holder-reads:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-dump-holder-reads:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-dump-holder-reads:b: Refuted: "A thread keeps its monitors while it parks, sleeps or reads a socket. Only `Object.wait()` gives up one."
recorded.prompt:q-dump-holder-reads:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-dump-holder-reads:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-dump-holder-reads:c: Refuted: the page shows a monitor cycle reported as "Found one Java-level deadlock". The reference table says Thread.print gives "a deadlock section for a cycle of monitors or of `ReentrantLock`s". With the hang, "there is no cycle: `reprice` waits for a latch, not a lock."
recorded.prompt:q-dump-holder-reads:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-dump-holder-reads:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-dump-holder-reads:d: The reason is refuted: with no deadlock section, "`restock` is just as stuck ... because there is no cycle". The holder's wait can be "a database call or an HTTP request without a timeout". FLAG, minor and partly true: if the socket read eventually returns, the requests would get through one by one. The page refutes d's reasoning (that no deadlock section means the monitor is passed on), not every outcome d predicts.
recorded.prompt:q-reentrantlock-recording:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-reentrantlock-recording:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-reentrantlock-recording:a: Refuted: the ReentrantLock waits were recorded as jdk.ThreadPark (park) events. The reference table says jdk.ThreadPark records "a park, such as a wait for a `ReentrantLock`".
recorded.prompt:q-reentrantlock-recording:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-reentrantlock-recording:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-reentrantlock-recording:b: Refuted: "a `ReentrantLock` is not a monitor ... recorded no `jdk.JavaMonitorEnter` events". The reference table says JavaMonitorEnter is "a wait to enter a `synchronized` block".
recorded.prompt:q-reentrantlock-recording:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-reentrantlock-recording:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-reentrantlock-recording:d: Refuted: "By default JFR records a monitor wait only from 20 ms up". The threshold drops the short waits, not the long ones. FLAG, partly true: d's conclusion ("may still cause waits") is the same as the correct option's. Only its reason is wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-container-default-heap:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-container-default-heap:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-container-default-heap:a: Refuted: in a container the memory the JVM sees "is the container's limit (`UseContainerSupport` is on by default)".
recorded.prompt:q-container-default-heap:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-container-default-heap:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-container-default-heap:c: Refuted: "`MaxRAMPercentage` defaults to 25". 75 % needs `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75`, which "gives 768 MB" for 1 GB.
recorded.prompt:q-container-default-heap:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-container-default-heap:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-container-default-heap:d: Refuted: "Without `-Xmx` the heap is 25 % of the memory the JVM sees". The flag table shows a fixed MaxHeapSize chosen without -Xmx, for example "With no flags in a 1 GB container the order service gets a 256 MB heap".
recorded.prompt:q-oomkilled-under-xmx:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-oomkilled-under-xmx:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-oomkilled-under-xmx:b: Refuted, but only implicitly: the page says "`-Xmx` limits the heap only" and the flag table calls -Xmx the "maximum ... heap". The page never says outright that -Xmx caps the heap at every moment rather than after a collection.
recorded.prompt:q-oomkilled-under-xmx:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-oomkilled-under-xmx:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-oomkilled-under-xmx:c: Refuted: "'Reserved' is address space and costs nothing. 'Committed' is memory the process may touch; the kernel charges each page to the container once it is touched." FLAG, minor: the "says" text claims "a container limit counts committed memory", but the page is more precise and says touched pages are charged.
recorded.prompt:q-oomkilled-under-xmx:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-oomkilled-under-xmx:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-oomkilled-under-xmx:d: Refuted: "The initial heap is 1/64 of the memory, at least 8 MB, and `-Xms` sets it". The table shows InitialHeapSize well below MaxHeapSize. FLAG: the "says" text claims "the heap stayed below 2 GB", but the stem only says the heap after each collection stayed below 2 GB. Before a collection the heap could have grown toward 3 GB. The "says" text overstates the stem.
